exposure: Refugee status (Syrian war refugees vs. non-Syrian nonrefugees)
cohort: Syrian war refugees (n = 356) and non-Syrian nonrefugees (n = 5836) giving birth between January 2015 and December 2018 at a tertiary care provider in Germany
finding: Syrian war refugee women had lower rates of cesarean section but higher rates of adolescent pregnancies and neonatal umbilical artery pH ≤7.0 at birth compared with non-Syrian nonrefugee women.
mod_finding: Women with previous cesarean section had similar odds of cesarean section in the current pregnancy irrespective of refugee status.
